2021_222_m092121bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education meeting held September 21, 2021 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, with Acting Vice President Wilson presiding in the absence of President Schmidt and Superintendent Machesky. The Board adopted resolutions 21-076 through 21-080, the most consequential being approval of the 2021-2026 Strategic Plan, built from more than 50 listening sessions and Board sessions on March 13, May 4 and September 7, 2021. Every vote carried with 6 yes, 0 no, Schmidt absent. Residents dominated non-agenda public comment with objections to and support for the district mask requirement.
2021_222_m092121bdmtg.page:
**Meeting and attendance**
Held September 21, 2021 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Acting Vice President Wilson called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; President Schmidt and Superintendent Machesky were not in attendance. Present with Dr. Wilson were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff and Philippart, plus administrators Birmingham, Carrier, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, Fulcher, Brinks, Cottone, DiPonio, Godfrey, Whan and West. Approximately 90 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 9:13 p.m.; Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, submitted the minutes.

**Recognitions**
Student representatives to the Board for 2021-2022 were introduced: Alyssa McLarty (Troy College & Career High School), Yara Mashal (International Academy - East), Sasha Palmkoeck (Athens High School) and Sarayu Bethamcherla (Troy High School). Mr. Fulcher and the Board recognized 2021 spring-sports all-state athletes Angela Anderanin, Elizabeth Bultynck, Alyssa Carnes, Zachary Hanoosh, Zachary LaRochelle, Abigail Mayne, Stephanie Ochoa, Sabrina Song and Tianhui Zhu. The Association of School Business Officials International awarded the district its Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020, crediting Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and Finance Director Kandice Moynihan. Bemis and Troy Union Elementary Schools, led by Principals Jeremey Whan and Mike Cottone, were honored as 2021 National Schools of Character, two of 47 schools nationally recognized by Character.org. Michigan Association of School Boards honors went to Vital Anne (Award of Merit), Elizabeth Hammond (Advocacy Skills Specialty Award) and Dr. Nancy Philippart (Data Skill Specialty Award), with the full Board earning the Honor Board Award and Standard of Excellence Award.

**Consent agenda (21-076)**
Moved by Hauff, supported by Gottlieb: approval of items A through D - minutes of the August 17, 2021 meeting; Treasurer's Report for July 2021; Troy Career Center Lease; and the Public Education Leaders Advocacy Institute & Professional Learning Seminar. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Schmidt.

**Personnel (21-077, 21-078)**
Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, reported on the hiring process and the factors driving annual teacher hiring: retirements and resignations, full-year leaves of absence, FTE status and student enrollment. Moved by Anne, supported by Philippart, the Board approved the elementary and secondary personnel recommendations including a large slate of new hires. The Board also issued a two-year administrative contract without tenure to Patrick Griffin, who begins transitioning into the Assistant Principal role at International Academy East on September 22, 2021.

**Strategic Plan 2026 (21-079)**
Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent for Elementary Instruction, presented the planning process and findings from over 50 listening sessions. The four pillars were refreshed: green Early Childhood to Career, red Equity and Well-Being, blue Deep Learning, gold Building Capacity, under the vision World Class for ALL. The adopting resolution (Philippart/Hammond) recited the March 13, 2021 winter retreat session, the May 4, 2021 workshop and the September 7, 2021 workshop that produced the final draft, and was adopted on the 21st day of September 2021.

**Business, public comment and other**
Rick West presented a 2013 Bond Work/Sinking Fund update covering summer capital projects - concrete, door and window replacement, fencing, flooring, paving, roofing and remodeling. Student representatives delivered building reports before public comment. Non-agenda speakers addressed masks, mask exemptions, critical race theory, curriculum materials and typing instruction. Under 21-080 the Board certified Vital Anne, Gary Hauff, Karl Schmidt and Nancy Philippart as delegates to the MASB 2021 Delegate Assembly on November 11, 2021. Next workshop: Tuesday, October 5 at 6:00 p.m.; next meeting: Tuesday, October 19 at 7:00 p.m.
2021_222_m092121bdmtg.verbose:
**Setting**
The Troy Board of Education met on September 21, 2021 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Acting Vice President Wilson called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. President Schmidt was not in attendance, nor was Superintendent Machesky. In addition to Dr. Wilson, Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff and Philippart were present. Administrators present were Birmingham, Carrier, DiPilato, Griffor, Harris, Fulcher, Brinks, Cottone, DiPonio, Godfrey, Whan and West. Approximately 90 members of the audience attended. Vice President Wilson opened with a statement describing how the evening's meeting would proceed in compliance with the Open Meetings Act and reviewed the guidelines for public comment.

**Student representatives introduced**
Dr. Wilson introduced the high school student representatives to the Board for the 2021-2022 school year. Alyssa McLarty of Troy College & Career High School, a senior and student athlete, led initiatives including a food pantry for TCCHS families, competes on the Athens swim team and dual enrolls at Oakland Community College. Yara Mashal, a junior at International Academy East, has served on student council and as a board member of the Insight Club and the Relay for Life Club, is fluent in Arabic, is studying French, has traveled to five continents and interned at Wayne State University's School of Medicine doing neurological research. Sasha Palmkoeck, a senior at Athens High School, is a lead dancer with Eisenhower Dance Detroit, works at Grabbagreen, and is a Summa Cum Laude, AP and NHS Scholar who will major in Behavioral Neuroscience. Sarayu Bethamcherla of Troy High School served on the district equity team, is a Youth Consultant with the NEP organization, is Vice President of the Troy StuGo Executive Board, sits on the Michigan Student Leadership Board of Delegates (an elite group of 30 students), was a DECA State Champion in Marketing Management Team Decision-Making, competed at DECA International, attended the Forbes Under 30 Summit and was accepted into the Students Demand Action Summer Leadership Academy.

**Athletic and institutional honors**
Mr. Fulcher and the Board recognized 2021 spring-sports all-state athletes: Angela Anderanin (Girls' Tennis), Elizabeth Bultynck (Girls' Soccer), Alyssa Carnes (Girls' Soccer), Zachary Hanoosh (Boys' Lacrosse), Zachary LaRochelle (Boys' Lacrosse), Abigail Mayne (Girls' Soccer), Stephanie Ochoa (Girls' Tennis), Sabrina Song (Girls' Tennis) and Tianhui Zhu (Girls' Tennis). The Association of School Business Officials International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting Program honored the Troy School District for the preparation and issuance of a high quality Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020; Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, and Kandice Moynihan, Finance Director, and their staff were credited. Bemis and Troy Union Elementary Schools were honored with the 2021 National Schools of Character Award, one of 47 schools across the country receiving the distinction from Character.org; Principals Jeremey Whan and Mike Cottone, along with a representative from each building, accepted awards from the Board. Michigan Association of School Boards honors were presented: Trustee Vital Anne earned the Award of Merit, requiring completion of all Level 1 courses and 45 education credits; Trustee Elizabeth Hammond received the Advocacy Skills Specialty Award; Trustee Dr. Nancy Philippart received the Data Skill Specialty Award; and the entire Board earned the Honor Board Award and the Standard of Excellence Award, the minutes noting seven Board members committed to life-long learning and positive policy making.

**Additions, deletions and agenda-item public comment**
There were no additions or deletions. Dr. Wilson reported that one Request to Address the Board had been submitted for agenda items by the same individual who submitted one for non-agenda items; because each individual is allowed 3 minutes for public comment, she combined the two requests.

**Consent agenda - resolution 21-076**
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mr. Gottlieb, the Board approved items A, B, C and D: minutes of the August 17, 2021 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report - July 2021; Troy Career Center Lease; and Public Education Leaders Advocacy Institute & Professional Learning Seminar. Yes: 6. No: 0. Absent: Schmidt.

**Personnel - staffing update and resolution 21-077**
Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, reported on the district's hiring process and the factors influencing the number of teachers hired each year, including retirements and resignations, full-year leaves of absence, FTE status and student enrollment. Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Philippart, the Board approved the personnel recommendations. The new hires were: Jordan Baines, Julia Barraco, Laura Beacom, Haley Beard, Lisa Brown, Meridith Cervenak, Julie Check, Alexis Chie, Chloe Church, Abigayle Cohen, Andre Collaku, Hannah Dadles, Sara Davis, Joseph D'Orazio, Lorraine D'Souza, Madison Edwards, Alana Esshaki, Duran Franklin, Padro Gould, Kaitlin Harrison, Sara Hawks, Jordan Held, Benjamin Hill, Nicholas Holevar, Lindsey Howard, Lindsey Huebner, Stephanie Indianer, Cody Jamieson, Meredith Jerome, Marina Karjo, Nancy Kast, Cindy Kaump, Sara Konja, Meghan Kosters, Emma Kowal, Sathyaja Krishnan-Nair, John Le, Trysta Lee, Megan Luther, Amanda Matousek, Kyle Maxson, Mary McClure, Messica McHale, Drew Melesky, Maria Mendola, Derek Mohamedally, Courtney Motherwell, Justin Nelson, Karoline Newer, Shane Norris, Jillian Pertler, Amanda Peters, Victoria Petrouneas, Jeena Philip, Tiffany Robinson, Megan Ross, David Said, Jennifer Said, Theresa Saporito, Andrew Scovoronski, Stephanie Smith, Emily Stetson, Melissa Strauss, Wendy Stuart, Vanessa Suarez-Manjarres, Jacquelyn Tindall, Bailey Tripp, Joanna Van Eizenga, Joseph Verhelle, Michelle Waak, Emily Walker, Elizabeth Waymaster, Isaac Weiss, Bethany Welc, McKenzie Wezeman, Raquel Winn, Kristen Withers, Seth Wyatt, Taylor Young, Allie Zawada and Fan Zhang. Yes: 6. No: 0. Absent: Schmidt.

**Administrative appointment - resolution 21-078**
Moved by Mr. Gottlieb and supported by Mrs. Hammond, the Board issued a two-year administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Mr. Patrick Griffin, who will begin transitioning his duties as Assistant Principal, International Academy East, starting September 22, 2021. Yes: 6. No: 0. Absent: Schmidt.

**Curriculum - Strategic Plan 2026 and resolution 21-079**
Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, presented a PowerPoint on the district's strategic planning process through 2026 and shared findings collected from over 50 listening sessions with students, parents, community members, staff and the Board. The mission and vision are being refreshed to enhance the pillars: the green pillar Early Childhood to Career will expand research with access through career; the red pillar Equity and Well-Being will focus on ensuring safety, belonging and connection; the blue pillar Deep Learning will center on ensuring learning for all throughout the system; and the gold pillar Building Capacity will expand to include students, staff and community as learners. The leadership team committed to the mission of ensuring learning for ALL, with the vision World Class for ALL and newly established goals in cultivating a collaborative culture, deepening learning and focusing direction. Background recited that in the 2015-2016 school year the Board joined the Superintendent and his team to introduce the vision of World Class 2020, whose Strategic Plan Pillars led the work across oneTROY for the last 5 years. Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Hammond, the resolution recited information-gathering interviews with the Board, Central Office administration, building administrators, teachers, professional and support staff, students, parents and community members; a strategic planning session during the Board's winter retreat on March 13, 2021; an additional workshop on May 4, 2021 that addressed key issues and priorities; and the September 7, 2021 workshop whose input produced the final draft. The Board approved the Strategic Plan 2021-2026 substantially in the form presented, as adopted on the 21st day of September 2021. Yes: 6. No: 0. Absent: Schmidt.

**Business - 2013 Bond Work/Sinking Fund update**
Rick West, Assistant Superintendent for Business Services, presented a PowerPoint updating the Board on capital projects completed over the summer, including concrete, door/window replacement, fencing, flooring, paving, roofing and remodeling, with photographs of the various sites. Board discussion followed.

**Student representative reports**
Dr. Wilson moved the student representative reports ahead of public comment because of the number of speakers, noting students would be dismissed after their reports. Alyssa McLarty (Troy College and Career High School), Yara Mashal (International Academy-East), Sasha Palmkoeck (Athens High School) and Sarayu Bethamcherla (Troy High School) each reported on events and activities at their schools.

**Public communication - non-agenda items**
Fabrice Smieliauskas, a Troy resident and TSD parent, addressed COVID safety protocols and thanked the district for requiring masks. Daniel Karg, an Athens High School alumnus, spoke on the importance of typing classes at the secondary level. Diana Magiera, a parent of two, spoke about a mask exemption for her son. Sarah Krieger, a parent of three, raised the effects of wearing masks and asked whom she could contact. Katie MacFarland raised concerns about critical race theory and Marxism in public schools. Ollie Apahidean raised concerns about teaching racism and books that promote division and hate. Joe Scott, a parent of two, cited social, emotional, academic and medical effects of children wearing masks. B. J. Lennon, a parent of three, called the mask mandate harmful and a personal choice for parents. Tracy Owens, a parent of three, raised concerns about the Summer Learning Resource letter about race and equity. Ryan Johnson, a parent of one, described attempts to have his son attend school without a mask and argued mandating masks violates the law.

**Other - resolution 21-080 and closing**
Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Anne, the Board certified that Mrs. Vital Anne, Mr. Gary Hauff, Mr. Karl Schmidt and Dr. Nancy Philippart will serve as delegates to the MASB 2021 Delegate Assembly on November 11, 2021. Yes: 6. No: 0. Absent: Schmidt. Ms. Griffor announced the next Board Workshop for Tuesday, October 5 at 6:00 p.m. in the Services Building and the next Board Meeting for Tuesday, October 19 at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building. The meeting adjourned at 9:13 p.m. Respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.

2021_223_troy_board_graph_presentation_2.paragraph: Year-end audit slide presentation to the Troy School District Board of Education for the year ended June 30, 2021, summarizing audit results, COVID-19 relief funding, fund-level results and enrollment trends. The financial statement audit produced an unmodified opinion and the federal program audit an unmodified opinion with no findings or questioned costs. General Fund revenue of $171,189,282 against expenditures of $164,655,892 carried the General Fund balance to $32,734,102, equal to 19.88% of total expenditures and other uses, or 73 days of operations.

**General Fund revenue and expenditures**
Revenue of $171,189,282 splits into state source revenue $109,711,606 (64%), local revenue $40,975,969 (24%), federal revenue $10,403,476 (6%) and interdistrict source revenue $10,098,231 (6%). Viewed by foundation components: state portion of the foundation allowance $82,370,147 (48%), property taxes $39,308,501 (23%), other state and local $39,107,158 (23%) and federal $10,403,476 (6%). Expenditures of $164,655,892 by object are salaries and employee benefits $134,891,405 (82%), purchased services $18,584,690 (11%), supplies $5,994,476 (4%) and other expenses $5,185,321 (3%). By function, direct instruction is 66.55% against an Oakland County FY20 average of 61.24%, followed by indirect instruction 13.80%, operations and maintenance 7.03%, school administration 5.47%, central services 1.75%, general administration and business services 1.72%, pupil transportation 1.72%, athletics 0.98%, debt service 0.60% and community services 0.38%.

**Enrollment, foundation and fund balance**
Troy's 2020-2021 foundation revenue per pupil of $9,315 sits mid-pack in Oakland County, below Bloomfield Hills $12,364, Birmingham $12,284, Southfield $11,331, Lamphere $10,789 and Farmington $10,405, and above West Bloomfield $9,156, Royal Oak $9,118, Novi $8,839, Walled Lake $8,675, Rochester $8,529, Waterford $8,134 and Huron Valley $8,111. Total state aid was $121,737,735 in 2020-2021. Fund balance as a percentage of expenditures ranged from 15.08% in FY2015 to 19.88% in FY2021.

**Outlook**
Public education funding for 2021-2022 items included the January 2022 Revenue Estimating Conference, state ESSER equalization funding with a $1,093 per pupil floor under the USED-approved state plan, the economic impact of the pandemic and MPSERS challenges; budgeting themes were strategic utilization of one-time federal and state funding, monitoring of pupil counts and a continued dynamic environment.
